US and Israel said to draft plans for resumed strikes on Iran after midterm elections
Times of Israel liveblog — 22 October 2026, 4:17 am (Israel time; 02:17 BST), citing The New York Times

According to the New York Times, the US and Israel have developed plans for renewed strikes on Iran following the US midterm elections on November 3. The countries have increased military training for "a short but intensive operation," including practice manoeuvres over Iraq to simulate strikes. Possible targets: energy facilities, nuclear sites, missile and drone arsenals. Officials believe another major offensive could significantly damage Iran's economy and compel diplomatic concessions. Trump could authorise strikes before November, though he might ultimately decide against military action.

(Search snippet, aggregated from NYT-based reporting:) The plans focus on a short, intensive operation that could last approximately three days. The American force, including three aircraft carriers, thousands of Marines, fighter jets and special operations forces, will not be fully in place until early November, when the hours of darkness over Iran also increase. Trump has not yet approved a new operation.
